Research proposal 01

Academic matching SaaS · Morocco

A clearer way to show
an academic decision

Six Behance references, three possible directions, and one proposed system for making the value of a personalized report easier to understand.

Recommendation

Use a typographic editorial base. Let the visual change with its job: expose the choice problem, explain personalization, make real evidence readable, or support a parent–student discussion.

Primary audience: Moroccan Campus France applicants. Parents are secondary. Business objective: purchase of the personalized report.

Research only

No Static Ad was created or modified. The existing Creative 01 V2 remains awaiting Imran. Selecting a visual direction is the next gate before any further production.

R1Study abroad / education agency

Study Abroad - Social Media Creative Ads Design

Inzamam Shawon

View actual Behance project

Make the subject unmistakable

Give Campus France one clear headline zone and group illustrative choices tightly. Replace destination spectacle with the actual academic decision. Do not import institutional logos, offers or claims.

Read art-direction analysis
Style & image treatment
Photographic education posters: architectural cutouts, students, restrained paper treatments, and distinct destination modules.
Typography & composition
Large destination or qualification headline above grouped details; sans-serif and condensed display forms. Font families unverified. The page's presentation montage is not a single ad.
Color system
Light neutral and pale blue/pink fields, dark green panels, and localized orange/red highlights. Borrow the limited roles, not these exact colors.
Strength
A recognisable subject and a strong first read survive changes in imagery. Consistent brand/footer anchors hold different compositions together.
Weakness
Logo arrays, small requirements, QR codes, flags and contact strips compete at feed size. Destination imagery can imply an agency service rather than academic matching.
Adapt for Match
Give Campus France one clear headline zone and group illustrative choices tightly. Replace destination spectacle with the actual academic decision. Do not import institutional logos, offers or claims.
Conversion relevance · hypothesis
Fast topic recognition can qualify attention. A clearer next action could support entry into Match; the reference provides no evidence of paid-report conversion.

Inspection scope: Cover, campaign montage and poster compositions inspected; selected montage saved. Useful for hierarchy, not proof or claims.

R2SaaS product advertising

Social Media - SaaS

Eduardo Richter and José Felipe Mondadori

View actual Behance project

Keep the pain and product connected

Keep one academic problem, one product explanation and one action. Use a compact, genuine report detail or a labelled educational relationship instead of decorative UI. Recolor to ProTrain's documented palette.

Read art-direction analysis
Style & image treatment
Billnest campaign combining typographic messages, human imagery, flat illustration and small invoice-status motifs.
Typography & composition
Conversational question first, short product explanation second; common logo and palette across different compositions. Clean sans-serif forms; font family unverified.
Color system
White, near-black plum and saturated violet. Violet-on-dark sections are less legible than white-on-dark sections.
Strength
The campaign varies the visual while preserving an identifiable brand. Small invoice events connect abstract automation to a concrete task.
Weakness
Some long hooks, dense support and decorative swashes weaken the first read. A generic laptop portrait alone does not prove the mechanism.
Adapt for Match
Keep one academic problem, one product explanation and one action. Use a compact, genuine report detail or a labelled educational relationship instead of decorative UI. Recolor to ProTrain's documented palette.
Conversion relevance · hypothesis
Task-specific language helps explain why a SaaS product matters. For Match, the equivalent is understanding why a formation fits, not an unsupported promise of admission.

Inspection scope: Cover and nine-post campaign grid inspected; two individual source posters saved. No product-performance data verified.

R3Software / editorial campaign system

Tecnologia & Software | Social Media

Carlos Pada ✪

View actual Behance project

Give every post a dominant message

Borrow the single-message discipline, alignment and quiet brand anchors. Use ProTrain forest and ivory, reserve amber for action, and replace chrome objects with meaningful choices or genuine evidence.

Read art-direction analysis
Style & image treatment
Nexustech editorial technology system: dark fields, oversized type, luminous green structures, 3D objects and alternate typographic compositions.
Typography & composition
An oversized headline is anchored to one side with subordinate explanation and a compact CTA. The wider grid changes scale while repeating small brand anchors. Font family unverified.
Color system
Near-black, white and bright green. Gradients and glossy objects create a technology mood rather than product evidence.
Strength
Strong light/dark hierarchy, a coherent campaign rhythm, and typography that can lead without relying on a face.
Weakness
Reflective abstract objects do not explain a product. Saturated green and small peripheral text can overwhelm; displayed percentages are not evidence for ProTrain.
Adapt for Match
Borrow the single-message discipline, alignment and quiet brand anchors. Use ProTrain forest and ivory, reserve amber for action, and replace chrome objects with meaningful choices or genuine evidence.
Conversion relevance · hypothesis
Distinct hierarchy can make the hook and action easier to find. Generic technology spectacle would weaken Match's explanation and should not be carried across.

Inspection scope: Cover, case-study text and multi-post campaign grid inspected; two individual posters saved. Publication date requires page recheck; not used to rank the work.

R4Modern education / Instagram presentation

Social Media Visuals for Education Brands

Emely Siraz

View actual Behance project

Make the supporting information findable

Use alignment or gaze to connect the existing student with the academic choices. Give the supporting message a high-contrast, readable area. Keep both visible at phone size.

Read art-direction analysis
Style & image treatment
A clean blue education poster with a compact information panel, a pointing student and generous separation between headline and supporting content.
Typography & composition
The destination is the largest line; the information panel creates a second reading stop. Script decoration is secondary. Typeface families unverified.
Color system
Deep blue content field, lighter blue surround, white type and a white information panel. A restrained palette gives the panel a clear role.
Strength
A person's gesture directs attention to specific information. The panel gives supporting content its own contrast and breathing room.
Weakness
The student still occupies substantial space. The action is small, and contact placeholders show a portfolio presentation rather than demonstrated live advertising.
Adapt for Match
Use alignment or gaze to connect the existing student with the academic choices. Give the supporting message a high-contrast, readable area. Keep both visible at phone size.
Conversion relevance · hypothesis
Findable explanatory content can help the viewer understand the next step. The small reference CTA is a limitation to correct, not a conversion pattern to repeat.

Inspection scope: Flat poster and Instagram/device presentations inspected. The repeated mockups show one core design, not a broad campaign system.

R5Learning campaign / typographic Instagram layouts

Design Studio | Creative Learning Campaign

SWWATI AMANNCHI

View actual Behance project

Let typography carry the composition

Borrow weight contrast, short fixed lines and a single purposeful emphasis. Keep ProTrain colors and the existing active scene; avoid eye bars, slanted Arabic, decorative arrows and broken Arabic word styling.

Read art-direction analysis
Style & image treatment
White space, black-and-white cutout photography, black typography and a single acid-green highlight; layouts adapt into carousel and device presentations.
Typography & composition
Short stacked phrases mix light and heavy sans-serif weights. One highlighted word creates emphasis; the same text modules rearrange across formats. Font family unverified.
Color system
Black, white, grey and electric lime. The system is memorable with very few color roles.
Strength
A headline can dominate without a large photographic background. The repeated type relationship remains recognisable across layouts.
Weakness
The stripe across the eyes, arrows and loose circles add decoration. Generic learning language and the passive presenter do not demonstrate a specific service.
Adapt for Match
Borrow weight contrast, short fixed lines and a single purposeful emphasis. Keep ProTrain colors and the existing active scene; avoid eye bars, slanted Arabic, decorative arrows and broken Arabic word styling.
Conversion relevance · hypothesis
A short typographic first read may improve comprehension in a feed. It still needs a specific mechanism or evidence to justify a paid report.

Inspection scope: Poster mockup, carousel arrangements and laptop/mobile presentations inspected. These are variations of one campaign message.

R6Education agency / bilingual brand system

Study Abroad Academy | Branding & Social Media

Mahmoud Khaled

View actual Behance project

Keep identity stable as compositions change

Define a stable corporate-logo/Match anchor, color roles and type pairing, then vary the composition by angle. Use ProTrain's supplied logo and Cairo/Poppins, not KAB artwork or its destination template.

Read art-direction analysis
Style & image treatment
KAB brand case study extending from palette and typography to print, website and a varied social campaign. Aspirational student/country composites share a consistent frame.
Typography & composition
The identity boards explicitly name Montserrat and Cairo. Social posts use large destination or question headlines and repeat a small top brand mark. This does not validate mixed-script ProTrain line order.
Color system
Deep blue and yellow lead, with supporting green/cyan documented in the case study. Social posts repeat blue/yellow and white framing.
Strength
Brand position, a limited palette and framing provide continuity without requiring an identical photo position on every post.
Weakness
Landmarks, planes and passive stock students make the work agency-like. Thin branding and long country names lose clarity when reduced; benefit lists become small.
Adapt for Match
Define a stable corporate-logo/Match anchor, color roles and type pairing, then vary the composition by angle. Use ProTrain's supplied logo and Cairo/Poppins, not KAB artwork or its destination template.
Conversion relevance · hypothesis
Campaign recognition can support continuity across exposures. Recognition alone does not establish trust, matching quality or purchases.

Inspection scope: Identity/color/type boards, print/web applications and social campaign inspected. This is a system reference rather than a model for direct-response proof.

02 / REVERSE ENGINEERING

Seven reusable principles

Translate visual observations into constraints. Keep the communication function; change the artwork, copy, palette and composition for Match.

Hook first

R1 separates subject from details; R2 gives the pain a clear first read. For Match, reserve a stable hook zone and use the owner's two explicit lines. Do not enlarge every text tier.

R1 · R2

Phone first

R4 makes an information panel easy to locate, but its small CTA is a warning. Inspect the actual 360 × 450 reduction and read the support and action without zooming. A desktop mockup cannot establish feed readability.

R4 · R5

Image with a job

R2 links some posts to a concrete task; R4 uses a gesture to direct attention. Match's student must actively compare or examine. A portrait, landmark or glossy object cannot stand in for the matching mechanism.

R2 · R4

One visible action

R3 separates the action from its explanation. Give Match one amber action area using the supplied wording; do not add QR codes, WhatsApp numbers and competing contact strips. The paid report remains distinct from the free entry offer.

R1 · R3

Contrast by role

R3 shows how light/dark contrast can lead a campaign; R5 uses one accent to focus the read. Match should use forest/ivory for reading and amber for action. Avoid white text on amber and avoid importing neon effects.

R3 · R5

Space between tasks

R4 separates headline, explanation and action. Use negative space to prevent those tasks colliding. Keep the explanation large enough to be useful; empty space is not a reason to shrink it.

R4 · R5

Stable identity, varied scenes

R6 maintains palette and brand position as compositions change; R2 varies illustration and typography. Fix Match's identity rules, not one rigid template. Confusion, mechanism, evidence and discussion need different visual structures.

R2 · R6

03 / THREE FUTURE DIRECTIONS

Different visual arguments,
one recognizable product

These are art-direction proposals, not newly produced ads or approved alternatives. The color blocks below describe material and hierarchy only.

Direction A · Recommended foundation

Editorial decision

Question leads
One meaningful scene
Action
Aesthetic
Calm, direct, academically credible. Large type and clear contrast with restrained photographic context.
Hierarchy & layout
A stable brand anchor, dominant hook, readable promise and one action, integrated around a compact decision scene. HOOK → PROMISE → CTA describes message functions, not mandatory visual bands. Text and image have deliberately unequal priority.
Image treatment
Retain the existing active student, laptop and illustrative cards for future C01 work. Reduce the scene's dominance; preserve gaze, hands and task.
Typography
Cairo for Arabic, Poppins for Latin. Controlled line breaks and isolated mixed-script runs. Weight contrast replaces extra decorative tiers.
Brand fit
Closest to documented forest, ivory, green and amber. Original logo remains intact with editable Match label.
Advantage
Strongest immediate fit to the actual V1 feedback. Easy to recognize across all four angles.
Limitation
Can become a text poster with a generic photo. Each angle still needs a meaningful visual relationship or genuine evidence.
Meta suitability
Clear first read in a 4:5 feed composition is plausible. Needs actual phone export review and later purchase testing.
Reference basis
R2 pain-led hierarchy + R3 editorial contrast + R5 typographic restraint; R1 supplies category recognition.
Direction B · Mechanism-led option

Visible reasoning

Profile context
Relationship
Explained choice
Aesthetic
Precise educational graphics with a small number of aligned labels and a single visible relationship.
Hierarchy & layout
A specific choice question leads; a simple profile-to-explanation relationship is central; support and action remain distinct.
Image treatment
Minimal photography. Use grouped academic inputs and choices as clearly labelled educational examples. Never imitate an undocumented product screen.
Typography
Cairo/Poppins with short labels and few levels. Keep Arabic right-aligned and French terms directionally isolated.
Brand fit
Green groups related information, ivory provides reading space, forest anchors the hook; amber remains the action color.
Advantage
Directly addresses the absent mechanism noted in PT02. Most useful for Personalized Matching.
Limitation
Can become a dense infographic. Real selection rules are not documented enough to invent causal links or matching scores.
Meta suitability
Useful only if one relationship is understandable at phone size. Recompose each format; do not miniaturize a full workflow.
Reference basis
R2 task/status motifs + R4 grouped explanation. This is an original synthesis, not a reproduced reference layout.
Direction C · Proof-led option

Evidence to examine

Real report crop
One useful annotation
Next step
Aesthetic
Documentary and practical: a genuine, readable excerpt is the main visual, with minimal annotation.
Hierarchy & layout
A short question introduces a large real excerpt. One annotation identifies the actual recommendation reason; the next action follows.
Image treatment
Use supplied report screenshots/PDFs unchanged in meaning. A parent/student scene may frame a shared reading task, not a testimonial.
Typography
Preserve real evidence typography. Add editable Cairo/Poppins captions around it, without recreating or inventing report content.
Brand fit
Ivory and white give evidence room; forest headings and the original corporate logo maintain the family resemblance.
Advantage
Makes the paid deliverable and its explanation inspectable. Best fit for Inside the Report and value objections.
Limitation
Genuine report assets are required. Tiny screenshots, decorative report covers and invented UI cannot satisfy proof.
Meta suitability
Promising for informed evaluation if the meaningful excerpt survives feed scale. Purchase effect remains unknown.
Reference basis
R4 information separation + R6 identity consistency. The proof requirement comes from ProTrain's brief and lessons, not a claimed screenshot in these references.

Choose A as the campaign foundation

It responds most directly to Imran's actual feedback: controlled hook reading order, less photo dominance, and a larger supporting message. Use B's explanatory logic when the angle needs a mechanism, and C's evidence discipline when the angle needs proof. This is one coherent system with purposeful compositional changes, rather than three unrelated styles mixed into each ad.

Why not make C the foundation now? The awareness creative is authorized to be illustrative, and the proof-led assets remain conditional. A provides a usable visual grammar without substituting invented evidence. This recommendation is strategic judgment, not a demonstrated conversion winner.

Type and reading order

الملف الدراسي
Choix de formations

Cairo + Poppins. Use the supplied local font files. Match visual weight across scripts rather than forcing identical numerical sizes. Never add Arabic letter spacing, skew Arabic words or split connected letters for emphasis.

For Creative 01, retain the exact current hook, promise and CTA from active-creative.json. Plan line breaks for that wording rather than copying the historical V2's line count. Isolate Arabic, French and punctuation runs. Inspect the rendered reading order from the right, including the question mark and the attachment around French terms.

Composition and proportions

Proposed starting point for later 1080 × 1350 work: approximately 60 px side margins, hook around 72–88 px, support around 48–56 px and action around 46–52 px. These are layout hypotheses, not universal legibility rules.

At 360 px width, the support range becomes approximately 16–19 px. Read the actual export. Resize or reflow when necessary; do not accept a nominal font size as proof.

Keep the visual subordinate to the argument. Use fewer cards, grouped more clearly, rather than shrinking the support to accommodate them. Lock the original logo aspect ratio and keep Match as editable type.

The four named angles in this research request are the current presentation framework. Do not treat their order as historical creative IDs. Historical proof-led creatives 03 and 06 still require genuine captures. No Creative 02 or alternative production begins before Imran's approval.

What V1 teaches this system

The active student makes the choice problem recognisable, but the photo band dominates the explanation. At phone size the support is noticeably quieter than the hook. The mixed-script terms and punctuation also need independent visual control.

The owner rejected V1's reading order and hierarchy despite earlier technical checks. Those checks remain historical evidence; they do not make V1 an approved reference. The separate profile-ad prototype was also rejected and is not a model for this system.

Current state: an existing V2 is already recorded as delivered and awaiting Imran. This report neither approves it nor revises it. V1 and V2 files and existing comparisons are preserved.

Offer discipline: two free formations are the entry action. The full personalized report is paid. A free-entry click or completed profile is not a report purchase.

05 / PRODUCTION RULES TO CARRY FORWARD

Ten decisions before export

Apply these only after Imran selects a direction and authorizes the next production step. Consult the retained project lessons again against the actual exported image.

Give the visual one job. Problem, mechanism, proof or shared discussion. Remove anything without a communication function.

Lock current Creative 01 wording. Preserve the exact latest hook, promise and two-free-program CTA from active-creative.json. Its current wording is documented and unrendered. Do not revive historical batch copy.

Control bilingual layout explicitly. Use editable text and isolated directional runs. Inspect shaping, punctuation, spacing and visual order in full and phone exports.

Read support at phone size. Inspect 1080 × 1350 and 360 × 450 outputs. A clear hook does not excuse a small explanation. Recompose other placements deliberately.

Keep the person active and secondary. Retain the existing C01 student/laptop/cards, while giving the explanation enough room. Do not replace the scene with a passive stock presenter.

Use original branding. Keep the supplied corporate logo unchanged, at its correct proportions. Match stays editable. Use documented Cairo/Poppins and the baseline palette.

Make one next step obvious. Amber with dark text; preserve the exact current action. No decorative arrows or competing contact/QR actions. Verify the actual destination before production.

Label illustrations and source proof. Conceptual cards are not matching results. Genuine report screenshots are required when the creative claims to show the product output.

Keep claims bounded. No price in the creative, admission guarantees, fabricated results, unsourced testimonials or invented statistics. Do not imply the full report is free.

Keep approvals and performance separate. Technical QA, Imran's creative approval and paid-purchase evidence are three different statuses. No publication or campaign launch from this report.

Later evaluation: after approval and launch authorization, judge paid-report purchases and acquisition cost with attribution defined. Track profile starts/completions as diagnostic steps. A higher click rate alone cannot establish the better purchase creative. Compare one intended visual variable at a time when running a controlled test.

06 / EVIDENCE & LIMITATIONS

What was actually inspected

The research supports art-direction choices. It does not establish the designers' clients, campaign delivery, local audience preference or sales performance.

Eleven actual project pages were opened. The six selected projects were inspected beyond their covers, including relevant posters, grids or identity applications. Browser-observed project images were saved with direct source URLs. No login, contact, appreciation, purchase or publication was required.

Selection emphasized reading hierarchy, a useful image role, adaptable campaign structure, brand fit and suitability for explaining a paid report. No numerical ranking or popularity score was used. Reference fonts are described visually unless explicitly documented; reference colors are qualitative observations. Exact ProTrain colors come from the local brand source.
